title: Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents
why: Flex-RSI benchmarks whether a frontier agent can use task feedback to revise its harness (prompts, tools, memory, control loop)—including the executor and the improver itself—not merely the task answer; paired runs attribute gains to harness edits. Core RSI / harness-evolution evaluation science. Official repo flex-rsi/rsi-bench (previously a paperless prototype) now matches this primary paper.
mechanism: Each run starts from the same general-purpose harness. An executor improves the task solution and keeps it only if held-out validation improves; an improver then revises the harness, including the executor and itself. Final solutions are scored on hidden test data under a fixed budget.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): closed-source and open-weight models on perception, reasoning, robot action, 3D reconstruction, visual creation, and infrastructure; self-improvement helps most when the agent builds its own solution; success/failure-only feedback holds back open-weight models; paired runs show that editing the harness itself contributes to the gains.

title: Divide, Diagnose, and Compose: Optimizing Agentic Pipelines and Harnesses
why: DeCAF automatically optimizes agentic pipelines and harnesses across prompts, topology, model selection, and tool policies via decomposed credit assignment, restricted-edit experiments, and a synthesizing trajectory evaluator—scaffold/harness optimization rather than weight training.
mechanism: Given a seed pipeline and benchmark, DeCAF identifies optimization dimensions and generates hypotheses; independent coding-agent sessions optimize each dimension under a restricted edit scope, recording hypotheses, edits, and outcomes (performance, cost, latency). A final synthesis session merges compatible findings and uses a component-level trajectory evaluator with role-specific rubrics to localize underperforming components.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across a diverse suite of agentic benchmarks, DeCAF improves average task performance by 2.58 percentage points while reducing inference cost by 4.30% and end-to-end latency by 42.45% versus the best overall baseline.

title: BOXBOX: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Running Performance Optimization
why: BOXBOX studies online recursive harness self-improvement during an ongoing open-ended task: the agent can revise its harness and hot-reload it without losing execution context, evaluated on PerfRace long-running software performance optimization—distinct from offline harness evolution that needs reference answers.
mechanism: Agent-triggered harness revision plus kernel-managed hot reloading that preserves execution context. Compared under matched test-time budgets with Frozen Harness, offline Harness Evolution, and Harness Scaling.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on PerfRace, BOXBOX achieves higher speedup with more efficient use of task time and model cost, reaching Speedup@4h of 1.70× versus 1.54× for the strongest baseline.

title: Recursively Self-Improving Electromagnetic Spectrum Agents: Architecture and Operation
why: Proposes RSI-ESAs that use operational feedback to update editable capabilities, then inherit retained task versions plus modification records and diagnostic knowledge into later rounds—domain recursive self-improvement with retained non-weight capability accumulation.
mechanism: Architecture of editable components plus a self-improvement process of problem diagnosis, candidate generation, validation, and inheritance. Effective task versions are retained; modification records and diagnostic knowledge guide subsequent updates so capabilities and improvement experience accumulate across rounds.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): a shared-spectrum scheduling case study illustrates improved task performance and capability accumulation over multiple improvement rounds under the tested conditions; open challenges are discussed for broader tasks and long-term operation.

title: FinEvolveKG: Controlled and Attributable Prompt Evolution for Financial Knowledge Graph Construction
why: Weight-free prompt evolution that mechanically confines GEPA, a reflective prompt optimizer, to a designated persona-policy block while keeping an approved general block byte-stable and separately versioned—attributable retained prompt optimization (GEPA instantiation) rather than monolithic unconstrained prompt rewrite.
mechanism: KG-construction harness separates reusable general and persona-policy prompt blocks and confines GEPA edits to the designated block. During persona adaptation the approved general block remains byte-stable; every optimizer edit is localized to a separately versioned persona policy. A dual objective balances generic temporal-KG quality with persona-relevant facts, motifs, and multi-hop connectivity.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): five mutation scopes on ticker-disjoint 10-K splits, three seeds for persona-conditioned arms across three personas. On the three-seed mean, the complete two-stage block-constrained workflow (v4) improves over the frozen prompt baseline (v1) by 19.4–30.9% and over unconstrained full-prompt workflow (v5) by 2.2–6.4%, winning all nine paired-seed comparisons; a blinded two-SME audit favors v4 over v5 in 70.1% of contrast-enriched judgments. Without further optimization, v4 also exceeds v5 on evaluated OOD shifts.

title: Decision Context: Persistent Behavioral Learning for AI Agents
why: Forge Decision Context compiles human corrections and self-assessed tool-call failures into retained imperative RULE directives injected at the decision points where they apply—procedural playbook/behavioral memory rather than factual retrieval, a reusable non-weight learning component.
mechanism: Captures behavioral signals from human corrections and self-assessed tool-call failures, compiles them into imperative RULE directives, and injects those rules at the decision points where they apply. The paper identifies representation, activation, and placement as central design choices for persistent behavioral learning.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): evaluated with four predecessor approaches on DC-Bench (71 scenarios across nine behavioral dimensions, built from real executed agent traces in a deterministic mocked-tool environment). forge_dc reaches 95% compliance versus 55% with naive retrieval while injecting approximately 10× fewer tokens per query.

title: AutoRefine: Auto-Calibrating Code Judges from Workflow Outcomes
why: Closed-loop recalibration of a deployable code-judge prompt from noisy development-workflow outcome labels (tests pass/fail, merge/abandon), with a teacher that explains kept labels or abstains—evaluator-prompt maintenance as the judged agent/system evolves (co-evolving judges / PromptOps-adjacent).
mechanism: A loop rewrites the judge prompt to reproduce workflow outcome labels. An informed teacher sees the judge's input plus the outcome, explains each label it keeps, and abstains when the outcome cannot be explained from what the judge sees—removing noisy labels and flagging cases that need better judge inputs rather than a better prompt.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on a held-out set with an execution oracle, calibration raised Scott's π from 0.36 to 0.60. With 25% randomly flipped fail labels on a deployed agent's outcomes, the teacher set aside flipped fail labels at more than twice the rate of genuine ones (overall noise 25%→20%). Recalibrating that agent's judge raised agreement with merge/abandon outcomes on 17 held-out current-workflow diffs (π 0.16→0.51); on 16 diffs from older workflows the previous judge stayed ahead, illustrating the need to recalibrate as the agent evolves.

title: A Controlled Study of Models, Skills, Feedback, and Curriculum in Agentic Robotics
why: Controlled evaluation of the self-learning loop in agentic robotics, where coding agents implement and iteratively improve robot policy code from physical-interaction feedback; systematically varies models, skill priors, feedback structure, and curriculum—evaluation science of self-improving agents (code as the retained non-weight object).
mechanism: Coding agents implement and iteratively improve robot policies from simulated and real-world physical interactions. A controlled simulation study spans nine manipulation tasks and systematically varies model capability, skill priors, feedback structure, and curriculum (631 experiment configurations, 28K coding-agent rollouts).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): the bottleneck is often not access to sufficient information but interpreting it into the right policy update. Across the studied factors, a successful self-learning loop depends on how effectively agents attribute failures, reason about task-relevant spatial and geometric structure, and selectively restructure code to improve policies.

title: When Feedback Becomes a Backdoor: Tracing Backdoor Skill Formation in Text-Space Skill Optimization
why: Security audit of text-space skill optimization (SkillOpt): poisoning reference-answer feedback can implant a persistent trigger-conditioned rule into retained Skill artifacts without access to the model, optimizer, or Skill file—negative-result / audit of skill-library evolution.
mechanism: Traces an attacker-supplied trigger–payload mapping from reflection to held-out activation under SkillOpt. Diagnostic interventions locate two successive bottlenecks: the Analyst abstracting away required literals, and edit-budget ranking removing exact edits before candidate construction even after literal preservation is enabled.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on SearchQA the natural attack retains an exact rule in all three seeds (each final Skill emits the payload on 200/200 triggered questions and 0/200 clean questions); in seed 42, removing the rule eliminates activation, with clean accuracy similar to benign SkillOpt (169/200 vs 171/200). On SpreadsheetBench, no natural run retains an exact rule across three seeds. Poisoned references can create persistent backdoors, but exposure alone does not ensure the induced rule is formed, selected, and retained.

title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
why: v2 consolidates the shared framework and adds the HarnessMM-V visual-agent study plus a public code repo, while restating the same HumanEval / DeepSeek Harness / MBPP token-saving results—experiment expansion of corpus HarnessMM v1 (guarded decision reuse + RSI of harness configs with frozen actor weights).
mechanism: RSI refines author prompts, context settings, and adapter rules from training feedback, with validation selecting deployment configurations. At inference, a controller reuses resolved decisions via Executable Decision Graphs, Guarded Decision Reuse, and Certified Callback Substitution while actor weights stay fixed. v2 additionally summarizes the HarnessMM-V visual-agent study and documents optimization overhead where measured.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (v2 abs): on HumanEval, preserves Codex success at 90.82% while reducing tokens per task from 66.72k to 47.02k (29.54% saving). For DeepSeek Harness, success improves from 71.43% to 85.71% while tokens decrease from 96.28k to 11.62k (87.93% saving). An MBPP ablation shows 26.91% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52% lower cost than retained callbacks. The report also summarizes the HarnessMM-V visual-agent study.

title: Continual Graph Memory and Community Infrastructure for AI-Assisted Mathematical Discovery
why: v2 retitles the work (was “Continual Graph Memory for Mathematical Research Agents”) and adds Ansatze, a community platform for inspecting, guiding, and checking the Ansatz research harness, with revised First Proof reporting (nine local verifier closures per two ten-problem batches; model-assessed outcomes distinguished from expert validation) and Lean formalization notes—method/presentation and experiment-reporting change versus corpus v1.
mechanism: Ansatz is a research harness whose continual graph memory separates model-accepted claims and dependencies from curated exploration. v2 adds Ansatze, a community platform connecting problem discovery, research records, manuscript analysis, and formal checking while preserving distinct evidence states.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (v2 abs): on First Proof, Ansatz recorded nine local verifier closures in each of two ten-problem batches; a partial result in the Second Batch also counted as a pass under the study’s criterion. These model-assessed outcomes include continued searches and differ from expert validation. Component studies and re-review expose disagreements and their dependency reach. Open-problem investigations produced candidate results, with five Lean formalizations reported. (Differs from v1’s “closure on all ten” / Jamison and Erdős problem claims.)
